main_text.p: הללהָלוֹךְ וְהִלְכוּ[?] Eundo & deficiendo, Genef.8.5. Imper. הִלְכוּ[?] Abite, Jer.51.50. Futur. יֵהָלֵךְ[?] Abit, Job.16.6. Et aliâ forma, תִּהְלַךְ[?] Ambulabit, Psal.37.9. Exod.9.23. ad formam תִּשְׁכַּב[?]. Niph.Praeter. נֵהֶלְכֹתִי[?] Abire, i.e. evanescere cogor, Psal.109.23. Pih.Praeter. הֵלְכוּ[?] Ire faciunt vel cogunt, Job.24.10. Fut. אֲהַלֵּךְ[?] Deduco, Prov.8.20. יְהַלֵּךְ[?] Praire faciet, Psal.85.14. Significat etiam simpliciter ut in Kal. Chald. Partic. מְהַלֵּךְ[?] Obambulans, Dan.4.26. Plur. ex Aphel, מְהַלְּכִין[?] Ambulantes, Dan.3.25. & 4. v.34. Hithp. הִתְהַלֵּךְ[?] Itavit, Obambulavit, Continenter, Indefinenter ivit: Praeter. הִתְהַלֵּךְ שָׁם[?] Itaverat eò vel illuc, 1.Sam.30.31.
הָלֵךְ[?] m. Itio, Ambulatio: Viator; pro אִישׁ הָלֵךְ[?] Vir itionis, 2.Sam.12.4. Fluxus; הָלֵךְ דָּבָשׁ[?] Fluxus mellis, 2.Sam.14.26. Quædam exemplaria in utroq; loco habent duplex Sægol.
הָלֵךְ[?] Chald. Vectigal, vel, ut Aben Esra scribit, מַס הַהֹלְכִים[?] Tributum transeuntium, Esr.4.13.
הָלִיךְ[?] m. Ambulatio, Incessus, Gressus: Plur. cum Aff. הֲלִיכַי[?] Gressus meos, Vestigia gressuum meorum, Job.29.6.

הֲלִיכָה[?] f. Idem: Aff. בְּהֲלִיכוֹתָם[?] In ambulatione sua, Nah. 2.v.5. quod juxta Masorethas scribitur cum ו redundante: Plural. הֲלִיכוֹת אֵלִי[?] Incessus Dei mei, Psalm.68.25. Aff. רָאוּ הֲלִיכוֹתֶיךָ[?] Viderunt incessus tuos, Ibid.
מְהַלָּךְ[?] m. Iter, Profectio: Constr. מְהַלַּךְ יוֹם אֶחָד[?] Itinere diei unius, Jon.3.4. Item, Ambulacrum, Ezech.42.4. Aff. מְהַלְכְּךָ[?] Iter tuum, Neh.2.6.
מְהַלְּכִים[?] m.p. Viæ, Ambulandi loca, Zach.3.7.
הלל[?] Infanivit: Partic. הוֹלְלִים[?] Infanientes, Psal.5.6. Futur. אַל תְּהֹלוּ[?] Ne infaniatis, Psal.75.5. Niph. Partic. וּבְכֹל הַנְּהֻלּוּלִים[?] Et in omnibus laudatus arboribus, Jesa.

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points and consonants are read from a small, slightly blurred scan. Every Hebrew form is marked [?] except where the letters were clear enough. The Hebrew of the first line (הָלוֹךְ וְהִלְכוּ) is uncertain. The lemma הלל in the left margin is set in large type and is treated as a margin note. The final "Jesa." is a citation ending the last entry, not a catchword. The page number 170 is read from a small heading figure and may be 179.
